title: A subclass's super call to a constructor the update reshaped
text: A mod class that extends a game class calls super(...) to a constructor the update reshaped or removed (1.17's EntityRenderer and LivingEntityRenderer taking an EntityRendererProvider.Context for the dispatcher, BlockEntityRenderer becoming an interface, 1.20.3's AbstractArrow). Three answers, each from the game's or Mixin's own files: a mixin's constructor super call, which Mixin never runs or resolves (Bytecode.findDelegateInit matches only owner and name, and only what follows the call is merged), goes to the reshaped constructor with each argument its type's zero, or to what the target extends now when the class became an interface (the mixin then implements it). A real subclass's constructor moves whole to take the new type in place of its parameter of the old one, as the game's own subclasses' constructors did (most of those that took the old type take the new one now), the old value read first as the game's code reads it (EntityRenderer's own two bodies line up dispatcher with context.getEntityRenderDispatcher(), followed up through MobRenderer and LivingEntityRenderer, which only pass it on); its super call is given the new value, and so is each call that makes the class from a moved lambda or override; a call with no new value at hand keeps the old constructor, whose super call stays reported. A mod class's constructor follows its mod superclass's that moved. An injector into a target's constructor the update reshaped is now checked too: by name alone with a handler taking the old constructor's arguments (Mixin refuses the descriptor), or by its old descriptor where the injector requires a place none of its selectors gives.
finish: the mods these breaks alone held link on 1.16.5 -> 1.17 and 1.20.2 -> 1.20.3 (both loaders), no update loses a mod on the full sweep, and the freed mods load in a real game
wrongIf: a freed mod fails in game at a rewritten constructor, or a moved constructor stores something other than what the old one did
result: 2026-11-23: cloud scoreboard 45151843168 against main 93080c5afa: every update 6,680 -> 6,677 of 9,423, big updates 2,517 -> 2,515, newest game 23 -> 23; 'call, game: linked' finishes 89 -> 77 and is in 1,507 -> 1,465 mods. Ten mods newly link (First-Person Model and Transparent on Fabric 1.17, Inventory Profiles Next and Polymorph on 1.19, Polymorph on 1.19.3, BadOptimizations and VMP on 1.19.4, ServerCore on NeoForge 1.20.3, ScalableLux on NeoForge 26.1) and thirteen false links are caught: mixins injecting into a constructor the update reshaped (Lithium and Visuality 1.20.3, Krypton 1.21.5 and 1.21.9, Animatica 1.21, Simple Voice Chat 1.19.1, PlayerAnimator 1.19.4, TerraBlender 26.1, Statement 1.15, e4mc-retro 1.16, FerriteCore 1.21.9 on both loaders). Freeing mixins' own super calls first let Lithium, Better Combat and Make Bubbles Pop link, and each crashed in a real client on exactly such an injector, which is why the check is here; main's own receipts show Animatica 1.21 and Krypton 1.21.9 failing the same way. FerriteCore 1.21.9 is the one over-report: its thread-detection mixin finds none of its three constructors, but its config plugin leaves it off unless asked, which the porter cannot see. In game (cloud-load 45126078282, 45126081509, 45132629326): Transparent loads on a real 1.17 server and client, VMP on a 1.19.4 server and client, BadOptimizations in a 1.19.4 client, ScalableLux on a 26.1 server and client, Inventory Profiles Next in a 1.19 client; First-Person Model (an EntityRenderDispatcher injector), Polymorph and ServerCore (a spawner injector) fail on mixins outside this change. Real subclasses move to the new context where the game's subclasses did (the self-test runs one on the JVM), but on Fabric 1.17 every renderer is made in a Fabric API EntityRendererRegistry.Factory lambda, and nothing before Fabric API 1.19.2 is read (maven's fabric-api jars for those releases carry no modules), so those constructors are kept and stay reported. Left: Fabric API before 1.19.2, constructors that gain values the old object never held (1.17's BlockEntity position and state), and mixin config plugins.
